legend: Given a board of size N×N%%ZSMJ0%%, where each cell can be alive, dead, or uninhabitable, simulate the evolution of the board for K%%ZSMJ1%% iterations based on the following rules:
∙%%ZSMJ2%% A live cell ('1'%%ZSMJ3%%) dies if it has an odd number of live neighbors.
∙%%ZSMJ4%% A dead cell ('0'%%ZSMJ5%%) becomes alive if it has an odd number of live neighbors.
∙%%ZSMJ6%% An uninhabitable cell ('#'%%ZSMJ7%%) never changes state and is never considered alive.
Each cell has up to 8 neighbors (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal).
Your goal is to determine the final state of the board after K%%ZSMJ8%% iterations.
input: The first line contains two integers N%%ZSMJ9%% and K%%ZSMJ10%% (2≤N≤8%%ZSMJ11%%, 1≤K≤109%%ZSMJ12%%) — the size of the board and the number of iterations.
The next N%%ZSMJ13%% lines contain N%%ZSMJ14%% characters each, describing the initial state of the board.
Let Si,j%%ZSMJ15%% be the character in the i%%ZSMJ16%%-th row and j%%ZSMJ17%%-th column:
∙%%ZSMJ18%% Si,j='1'%%ZSMJ19%% if the cell is alive,
∙%%ZSMJ20%% Si,j='0'%%ZSMJ21%% if the cell is dead,
∙%%ZSMJ22%% Si,j='#'%%ZSMJ23%% if the cell is uninhabitable.
output: Print N%%ZSMJ24%% lines, each containing N%%ZSMJ25%% characters, representing the final state of the board after K%%ZSMJ26%% iterations.
